every/recap: Chained slopes found the slope of z equals three x plus one, squared, at x equals one: the local slopes three and eight, multiplied, make twenty four.
every/every: But that took a fresh round of numbers for a single point. Slide x along the curve, and the slope keeps changing. Is there one formula for it, at every x?
every/expand: This one you could multiply out first, then use the power rule. But e to the x squared cannot be multiplied out, and neither can ln of two x plus three.
every/leibniz: Earlier methods for slopes had to untangle a formula first, clearing out its fractions and roots. Leibniz's 1684 paper, the one that named d x, promised a method that skips the untangling: it handles the pieces one at a time.
formula/letter: Do what the chain did, but keep u as a letter instead of a number. The inside, three x plus one, has slope three, wherever x is.
formula/outer: The outside, u squared, has slope two u. Leave it in u.
formula/times: Multiply them, as the chain rule says: two u times three is six u.
formula/sub: But six u is still in u. Put the inside back in for u: d z, d x is six times, three x plus one, a formula in x.
formula/notx: It is the inside that goes back in, not x alone: the outside only ever sees u.
formula/check: At x equals one, the inside is four, and six times four is twenty four: the slope found before.
formula/slide: And it holds at every x. Slide x along the curve, and six times, three x plus one, matches the slope measured there, all the way.
bend/seen: You have used this rule before, without its name: e to the three x became three e to the three x.
bend/why: Its inside, three x, has slope three. Its outside, e to the u, is its own slope. Multiply, and the three comes out in front.
bend/in: The inside need not be a line. In e to the x squared, the inside is x squared, whose slope, two x, changes with x.
bend/out: The outside is e to the u, whose slope is e to the u.
bend/res: Multiply, e to the u times two x, and put x squared back in for u: d z, d x is two x, e to the x squared.
worked/p1: Try one. What is the derivative of ln of two x plus three? Call it z.
worked/in1: The inside is u equals two x plus three, with slope two.
worked/out1: The outside is ln u, whose slope is one over u.
worked/a1: Multiply: one over u, times two, is two over u.
worked/back: Put the inside back in for u: d z, d x is two over, two x plus three.
worked/at: At x equals one, the inside is five, so the slope there is two over five: zero point four.
